pool.text: Norman invasion of Ireland launched from Wales
Henry II affirmed sovereignty, proclaimed himself Lord of Ireland
Dublin Castle founded as defensive work on orders of King John
Black Death struck Dublin, killing thousands over the next decade
Queen Elizabeth I established Protestant Trinity College
Local dignitaries ordered to oversee a lecture in Irish in Dublin.
The Gate founded to promote European and American avant‑garde works
The Dublin Marathon began to be held each October.
RDS hosted the Show Jumping World Championships during the Dublin Horse Show.
The Women's Mini Marathon started running each first Monday in June.
Approximately 150 acres of derelict land earmarked for development
International Financial Services Centre established, boosting financial services
City celebrated its official millennium marking settlement in 988
Dublin Institute of Design founded
Aviva Stadium hosted the Heineken Cup final for the first time.
Dublin Institute of Technology began a bachelor's degree in culinary skills.
College Park hosted Ireland's first women's Test cricket match against Pakistan.
Kevin Thornton received two Michelin stars for his restaurant.
Stainless‑steel conical spire completed on O'Connell Street
Morton Stadium held athletics events for the Special Olympics.
